title: Best Pizza in Seattle
dek: Neapolitan, New York, Detroit, tavern, and the squares.
intro:
Neapolitan, New York, Detroit, tavern, and the squares. Delancey and Dino's Tomato Pie are the argument. Everyone else is what you eat when the oven you wanted is slammed or you are on the wrong side of the water.

Judge a pie by the underside: blister, salt, and whether the middle survives the trip to the table. Styles sit next to each other because that is how the city actually eats, from a wood oven to a square slice on a paper plate.

entries.pullQuote: A wood oven in Ballard, and a pie that is the entire reason to go.
entries.blurb: Delancey is a Ballard pizzeria organized around a wood-fired pie. Order a whole pizza and eat it while the crust still crackles. The room is small, the oven is the point, and a salad is only there so you can claim balance. Share one pie before you start negotiating a second.

title: Belltown
dek: Where to eat and drink in Belltown, from a weeknight to a night you bothered to dress for.
intro:
Belltown eats well if you let it. Sushi by Scratch Restaurants and Shomon cover the cravings, and the walks between them are short enough to stay hungry.

Same craving does not get to take over the page. A neighborhood should feel like a week of dinners, not one cuisine copied down the block.

title: Gusto's 25
dek: Twenty-five dining rooms for when dinner should feel like an event.
intro:
Twenty-five rooms for when dinner should feel like an event, spread across the city so you do not eat the same night twice. AA Sushi and Bé Mi are the ones to remember. The rest of the list is how you eat through Ballard, Pioneer Square, Capitol Hill without repeating yourself.

Come hungry and order the obvious thing. Ballard, Pioneer Square, Capitol Hill will still be there when you want to get weird on the second visit.
